description: Eight rows, each one knob and four moves: step the running voltage up or down by the knob, or jump it straight to the knob or to minus the knob

params.text: Sets that row's value, 0V to 10V: a step size while the row is on add, a target while it is on jump
Chooses what that row's two sides do: add moves the output by the knob, jump sets it to the knob
Fires that row with its value as it stands, by hand
Fires that row with its value negated, by hand
Chooses what the output is held to: 0 to 10 V, ±5 V, ±10 V or no clip
Sends the output to 0V, by hand

inputs.text: A rising edge fires that row with its value as it stands
A rising edge fires that row with its value negated
A rising edge sends the output to 0V

outputs.text: The running value, with a lamp that reads green above zero and red below

notes: nothing moves on its own. The output holds whatever it was last set to until a button is pressed or an edge arrives.
where two rows fire on the same sample the last one in reading order wins, so a run of overlapping gates plays one row rather than a mixture.
the knobs are square-law: both ends are exact, 0V and 10V, but a volt is about a third of the way round and a tenth of a volt a tenth of the way.
out of the box the rows are a ladder from fine to coarse, 0.05V, 0.1V, 0.25V, 0.5V, 1V, 2V, 3V and 5V, with every switch on add.
